FIELD REFERENCE

Marlin fish: species identification and trip rules

Marlin is a group name, not one fish species. Blue, black, striped and white marlin differ in fin shape, body pattern and ocean range. Compare several features before naming a fish. For a fishing trip, identify the target species first, then check the local permit, measurement method and current retention rules.

Compare Blue marlin, Black marlin, Striped marlin, Atlantic white marlin before you choose a trip.

Updated 2026-11-23 · Castward

Which marlin species are you looking at?

Key factDetail
Blue marlinMakaira nigricans; pectoral fins fold against the body; pointed front dorsal fin
Black marlinIstiompax indica; rigid pectoral fins in fish over about 20 kg
Striped marlinKajikia audax; tall dorsal fin and visible vertical stripes; Pacific and Indian oceans
White marlinKajikia albida; rounded fin tips; Atlantic Ocean; compare roundscale spearfish
U.S. Atlantic blue marlin minimum99 inches, lower-jaw fork length; current restrictions also apply
U.S. Atlantic white marlin minimum66 inches, lower-jaw fork length; current restrictions also apply
Private U.S. Atlantic vessel permitHMS Angling permit: USD 24 application fee; annual renewal
Striped marlin size referenceNOAA lists 250–450 lb in its quick facts; not a promised catch weight

How do you separate black, blue and striped marlin?

Compare the pectoral fins and the height of the first dorsal fin. GFAA describes rigid pectoral fins in black marlin over about 20 kg, while blue and striped marlin can fold theirs against the body. Striped marlin have a particularly tall dorsal fin. Check several traits together, especially on small fish.

Read the source

Are white marlin, sailfish and swordfish the same fish?

No. White marlin have rounded fin tips and can resemble roundscale spearfish. Sailfish have a much larger, sail-like dorsal fin. Adult swordfish have a broad, flat bill and lack pelvic fins. Use the whole fish and its location for identification; a pointed bill alone does not identify a marlin.

Read the source

Which ocean should you choose for a striped marlin trip?

Striped marlin occur in the tropical and subtropical Pacific and Indian oceans. NOAA describes them around the Baja Peninsula and off southern California, among other areas. Choose a specific port and travel month before comparing trips. A species-wide range is too broad to establish a local season or likely catch.

Read the source

Which permit covers an Atlantic marlin trip?

For U.S. Atlantic billfish, NOAA requires an HMS Angling or HMS Charterboat/Headboat vessel permit. That permit covers the people fishing aboard the vessel. Ask the captain which permit covers the planned trip, then check any separate state requirements. A private HMS Angling permit requires annual renewal and has a USD 24 application fee.

Read the source

Can you keep a marlin in the U.S. Atlantic?

Check NOAA’s live fishery status before departure. Its minimum sizes are 99 inches for blue marlin and 66 inches for white marlin, measured from the lower jaw to the tail fork. A shared annual U.S. landings limit and shark-related restrictions also apply. These numbers are not a worldwide marlin rule.

Read the source

What should you know about marlin?

Does every marlin have the same scientific name?

No. Marlin covers several species. The table separates blue, black, striped and white marlin.

Do stripes prove that a fish is a striped marlin?

No. Blue and black marlin can also show body markings. Compare fin shape and other features.

What is lower-jaw fork length?

Measure in a straight line from the tip of the lower jaw to the fork of the tail. Do not include the upper bill.

Is a white marlin a small blue marlin?

No. It is a separate species with different identification features.

Is there one best month for marlin everywhere?

No single month fits every ocean and species. Choose the port and species, then check local seasonal information and current regulations.

Can a private HMS Angling vessel sell its marlin catch?

No. NOAA states that vessels with an HMS Angling permit may not sell their catch.
